note: Personas are fictional composites built from the Betsy questionnaire (14 answers, 16-19 Nov 2026), the coworking café conversation (24 Nov 2026) and the competitor analysis. 'form' = count out of 14 respondents; 'assumption' = not measured yet.

personas.name: Mark de Vries
personas.day: Cooks every service. Orders at the end of the shift, around 22:30, standing in the kitchen with his phone.
how_he_buys: Looks at shelves and fridges to decide what to order (form: 12/14)
Orders by WhatsApp and phone; webshop only for the wholesaler (form: WhatsApp 11/14)
6 suppliers, about one order per working day (form: 6-10 orders a week, 8/14)
Spends 3-5 hours a week on ordering, deliveries and invoices (form: 8/14)
pains: Has to be physically there to see what is missing
Delivery errors he only notices during service (form: monthly or more, 6/14)
A forgotten cut-off means a supermarket run the next day (form: monthly or more, 5/14)
will_not_give_up: The final say on every order (form: send alone OK for only 2/14)
His butcher and greengrocer: agreements made in person (open answers)
personas.wants_from_betsy: A ready order he can approve in one tap, with the reason next to every line.
personas.quote: I want to keep control. Just tell me what's missing and why.

personas.name: Sanne Peeters
personas.day: Behind the counter from opening. Does the admin between the lunch rush and closing; orders for the next day before the bakery's 14:00 cut-off.
how_she_buys: Fewer suppliers than a restaurant (5), but daily fresh products: bakery and milk every day
Demand moves with weather and events on the square (assumption)
Fixed prices with her coffee roaster through a contract that includes the espresso machine
pains: Croissants left over on quiet days, sold out by 10:00 on busy ones (assumption, to validate)
Counting milk and oat milk every afternoon
Short deliveries from the bakery that still appear on the invoice
will_not_give_up: Her roaster contract: price comparison on coffee is pointless
personas.wants_from_betsy: The daily list prepared without asking, so she only checks and sends.
personas.quote: Make the list for me. I'll look at it before I send it.

personas.name: Youssef Amrani
personas.day: Closes the kitchen on the evenings Mark is not there and receives deliveries in the morning.
how_he_buys: Counts stock and receives deliveries; does not order (form: who orders 'it changes' in 3/14)
pains: Does not know the agreed prices, so cannot judge a delivery note
personas.wants_from_betsy: Send the count in one message and know immediately whether a delivery is complete.
personas.quote: I just want to send the count and go home.

ideal_profiles.title: Ideal restaurant

criteria.label: Who buys
criteria.value: Owner or owner-chef, on a phone, after service

criteria.label: Suppliers
criteria.value: 3-8: produce, meat, fish, dairy, wholesaler, drinks

criteria.label: Order rhythm
criteria.value: 6-10 orders a week, each supplier with its own cut-off

criteria.label: Agreements
criteria.value: At least one contracted or personal supplier

good_fit_signals: Supermarket runs or stockouts at least monthly
Owner wants suggestions but keeps the send button
not_a_fit: Kitchens already on stock software with suggested orders (Apicbase, MarketMan, Nory)

ideal_profiles.title: Ideal café or bar

criteria.label: Ownership
criteria.evidence: form 5/14 are cafés or bars, all independent

criteria.label: Order rhythm
criteria.value: Daily for bakery and milk, weekly for the rest

criteria.label: Stock data
criteria.value: None or the ordering portal of one supplier
criteria.evidence: café case: AI on the ordering portal, checked by hand

criteria.label: Channel
criteria.value: WhatsApp, webshop, email to the roaster

criteria.label: Agreements
criteria.value: Coffee contract with machine on loan

good_fit_signals: Daily fresh products thrown away or sold out
Already trying AI for ordering (the coworking café)
not_a_fit: Bars with a full drinks-only supply contract (nothing to decide)

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want to send my stock count as one quick message after service, so that I don't have to fill in a form or open an app.
acceptance: Free text in English or Dutch is turned into a table of product and quantity
Words like 'ok' or 'plenty' mean no order is needed
Anything unclear gets one short question, not a guess
Mark sees the parsed table before anything else happens

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want a reminder before a supplier's cut-off when a product is running low, so that I don't end up at the supermarket the next day.
acceptance: The reminder comes before the cut-off of the next delivery day
It names the products below their reorder level
No reminder when stock is fine

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want one order proposal per supplier with a reason on every line, so that I can check it in seconds.
acceptance: Quantity brings the product back to par
Each line has a one-sentence reason and the data it used
Orders below a supplier's minimum are flagged with the fee

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want to approve, edit or reject every order, so that nothing reaches a supplier without me.
acceptance: Approve, edit and reject are always available
An edited order is shown again before sending
Without explicit approval the status stays 'draft'

user_stories.story: As an owner with agreements with my butcher and greengrocer, I want Betsy to always order from them, so that my relationships and contracts are respected.
acceptance: A contracted or preferred supplier is never replaced
When a rule comes from a document, Betsy cites it (e.g. DOC-03)

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want to see when another supplier is cheaper, so that I can bring it up with my supplier myself.
acceptance: The difference is shown as information next to the line
The proposal itself does not change supplier

user_stories.story: As a shift lead receiving a delivery, I want it compared with the order, so that missing or wrong items are reported the same day.
acceptance: Missing quantities and wrong items are listed per line
The supplier's claim deadline is shown (e.g. 24 h for Hendriks)
A claim message is drafted, sent only after the owner approves

user_stories.story: As an owner-chef, I want invoices checked against the order, the delivery and the agreed prices, so that I don't pay for what I didn't get.
acceptance: Flags price above agreement, billed but not delivered, and duplicate invoice numbers
Each flag shows the amount at stake
No dispute is sent without approval

user_stories.story: As a café owner, I want tomorrow's bakery order adjusted to what I tell Betsy about the day, so that I sell out less and throw away less.
acceptance: Starts from the usual need for that weekday
Uses signals in the message (leftovers, a market, rain) and quotes them as the reason
Arrives before the bakery's 14:00 cut-off

user_stories.story: As a café owner, I want Betsy to work in Dutch with my own suppliers and rules, so that it fits my café and not a restaurant.
acceptance: Messages and proposals in the profile's language
Same agents, different profile: no code change between Vonk and Kiem

user_stories.story: As a café owner, I want to choose per action what Betsy may do alone, so that it prepares my list without asking but never sends it.
acceptance: Each action has a mode: alone, approval or never
Kiem: suggest = alone, send = approval, compare prices = never

user_stories.story: As a shift lead, I want to send counts without being able to approve orders, so that the owner keeps control even when I'm closing.
acceptance: Counts from staff update stock
A staff message asking to skip approval is ignored and the owner is asked

user_stories.story: As an owner, I want text inside invoices and supplier documents never to change what Betsy does, so that nobody can order on my behalf by writing a note.
acceptance: Instructions found in documents are treated as data
The three injection cases (INJ-01 to INJ-03) pass

user_stories.story: As the developer of Betsy, I want every run traced and measured on the scenario set, so that I can choose models and prove the team beats the single agent.
acceptance: Each run records agent, tools, model, tokens, cost, latency and outcome
The dashboard compares models and agents on the same 15 scenarios
